edges.description: Incorrectly translated mitochondrial proteins are proposed to impair respiratory function. The hybrid-ribosome study does not itself measure human respiratory complexes or prove mediation in cochlear cells.

Reduced synthesis of mitochondrial respiratory-chain components is a proposed route to impaired respiration. Supporting family-cell studies show both abnormalities, but do not isolate each mediator in human hair cells.
Respiratory impairment is proposed to reduce mitochondrial ATP output. The measured mitochondrial ATP condition suppressed glycolysis; it does not demonstrate the same loss of total cellular ATP.
Mitochondrial dysfunction may increase oxidant stress or reduce stress resistance. The selected cell studies and general drug models do not establish a uniform ROS mechanism in carrier cochleae.
Energy limitation could compromise mitochondrial integrity and activate downstream cell-death pathways. Its necessity or sufficiency for MT-RNR1-associated human hearing loss remains unresolved.

Oxidant injury can contribute to sensory-cell death, but the complete mitochondrial-variant-to-hair-cell pathway remains hypothetical. Antioxidant protection in one drug model does not establish a universal route.

Loss of sensory transduction contributes to persistent sensorineural hearing loss. Clinical laterality and severity are documented in affected humans; the tissue mechanism is supported mainly by general ototoxicity models.

Preferential basal-cochlear injury offers an anatomical explanation for high-frequency loss in general aminoglycoside toxicity. Carrier audiograms are variable, so this is not a required sequence for every affected individual.
Defective thiolation is proposed to impair tRNA stability and lower steady-state abundance. Northern blots measure abundance, without directly measuring degradation kinetics.

Lower availability of mitochondrial tRNAs can impair translation. The same family-derived lines show reduced mitochondrial protein labeling, but the contributions of thiolation, abundance and other background effects were not independently rescued.
Drug distribution into the inner ear and entry through hair-cell membranes precede intracellular accumulation.
